chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:
The jurist al-'Askari عليه السلام said: “There is no mouth-rinsing nor nose-inhaling in ghusl or in wudu (ablution).”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The correct way to understand these reports is that mouth-rinsing and nose-inhaling are not among the obligatory acts of wudu; rather, they are among the recommended acts. And that which indicates that both of them are recommended in the ghusl of janabah.

key_terms.اسْتِنْشَاقٌ: drawing water into the nose during purification
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath, discussed here in the context of purification from janabah
key_terms.الْمَسْنُونَاتِ: recommended sunnah acts that are not obligatory
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath performed due to the state of janabah
key_terms.مَضْمَضَةٌ: rinsing the mouth as part of purification practices

ai.seo_question: Are mouth-rinsing and nose-inhaling obligatory in ghusl and wudu according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that mouth-rinsing and nose-inhaling are not obligatory parts of ghusl or wudu (ablution). The concluding statement explains that these acts are to be understood as recommended sunnah acts rather than legal obligations, especially in the ghusl of janabah.
